15	# FigJam Type - Process
16	
17	A process is work that moves through steps, decisions and often several people or teams: a refund, an approval, a release, an onboarding checklist, a decision tree. It is a flowchart marked `%% type: process`, so the check holds it to process rules rather than user-flow rules.
18	
19	**Loading Condition:** CONDITIONAL, when the Flow route draws a process or decision flowchart
20	**Purpose:** The grammar, rules, budget and read-back for a process
21	**Pairs With:** `assets/templates/process.md`
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 1. WHEN TO USE
26	
27	**The reader's question:** who does what, in which order, and where does the work change hands?
28	
29	- A process across teams or roles, drawn with one lane per actor
30	- A decision tree or a pipeline with no actors, drawn without lanes
31	- A process that reads from or writes to a store, or takes data in and hands data out
32	
33	Use a user flow when the subject is one person's screens, a state diagram when one thing moves between named states, and a sequence when the order of messages between systems is the point.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## 2. WHAT THE BOARD DRAWS
38	
39	```text
40	%% type: process
41	flowchart LR
42	```
43	
44	The first line of the block names the type for the check, and the composer reads it too. A process runs `LR` or `TD`.
45	
46	| Shape | Mermaid | Means |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| Stadium | `id([Label])` | Start or end |
49	| Rectangle | `id[Label]` | A step |
50	| Rhombus | `id{Label?}` | A decision |
51	| Circle | `id((.))` | A merge dot |
52	| Cylinder | `id[(Label)]` | A store, such as a database or a log table steps read and write |
53	| Subroutine | `id[[Label]]` | A step that is a process of its own, drawn elsewhere |
54	| Parallelogram | `id[/Label/]` | Data entering or leaving, such as a form or a report |
55	
56	The last three come from Figma's list of shapes that render as distinct FigJam shapes, and translate sk-design-diagram's input and output chips. Every other Mermaid shape falls back to a plain rectangle or adds a meaning the reader has to learn.
57	
58	A lane is a subgraph with a readable label, `subgraph agent ["CS agent"]`, holding the steps that actor performs.
59	
60	**Status lane.** When the parties move one shared record through named statuses, such as an order or a commission, a laned process may give those statuses a lane of their own. `%% status: <lane id>` names it. The lane is declared first, so the board draws it on top, and holds each status as a plain node `id[Label]`, joined in order by `-->` from the first status to the last. A step that moves the record to a status draws a dotted `-.->` into that status. The status lane is never an actor lane: no work happens in it, a status never leads to a step, and its states and connectors count toward the budget.
61	
62	```text
63	%% status: status
64	subgraph status ["Order status"]
65	    placed[Placed]
66	    shipped[Shipped]
67	end
68	placed --> shipped
69	ship -.-> shipped
70	```
71	
72	**Detail cards.** At the `Balanced` and `Faithful` detail levels a step may carry a body under its one-line label, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 4 sets out: `%% level: balanced` or `%% level: faithful` once, then one `%% detail: <step id> | <line> | <line>` line per step.
73	
74	**Notes.** A `%% about: <lane id or zone label> | <line> | <line>` line puts up to three note lines under a lane's or a zone's title, such as how long that party has to act. A process without lanes and with two or more `%% zone:` stages gives every zone notes, `Starts:`, `Ends:` and `Good to know:` where the source holds them, unless it runs at `Simplified`.
75	
76	Connectors are `-->` for the flow and `-.->` for an optional or proposed step. A log write that runs today is drawn solid. A source that says every decision or every step is logged names those nodes as its writers, so the log store is drawn with one solid edge from the decision the reader most needs and the source line says the others write it too.
77	
78	On the board the status lane draws each status as a white chevron, joined by the status line, and each move as a dotted gray line the key names `Moves the status`. A step with a body is a card: its label in Bold on one line, a spacer and the body left-aligned under it. On the board each lane is a band in a light tint, named after its label, stacked in the order the model declares them, and every step sits inside its lane's band. The kinds take their shapes from `references/style-guide.md` Section 2 and their colour roles from `assets/figjam-design.md`: a store is a cylinder in the `store` role, data entering or leaving a parallelogram in the `io` role and a sub-process a predefined-process shape in the `neutral` role. A process without lanes may group its steps into stages with `%% zone:` lines.
79	
80	---
81	
82	## 3. RULES
83	
84	The check enforces:
85	
86	- **The seven shapes above only**
87	- **Decisions have 1 to 3 labelled exits,** and a merge dot carries no words
88	- **Every step has a way in and a way out,** a stadium only starts or ends, and a store or a data shape needs one connector
89	- **`-->` or `-.->` only.** A thick connector competes with the marked step, and a headless or two-way one hides the direction work moves in
90	- **Lanes, when used, number 2 to 6,** never nest, each hold a step, and every step sits in one. A connector joins steps, never a lane
91	- **A lane takes the neutral pair** `fill:#F5F5F5,stroke:#B3B3B3` or no style at all, and never counts as the accent. The composer tints lanes itself, so a lane style changes nothing on the board
92	- **Without lanes, at most 9 nodes and 12 connectors. With lanes, at most 12 and 16,** sk-design-diagram's process budget and its balanced detail level. **A laned process at `Faithful` with detail cards reads at 18 and 24**, because a step's body carries what would otherwise be cut
93	- **A status lane, when used, is one lane,** named by one `%% status:` line, declared first, holding two or more statuses as plain `[Label]` nodes in a single `-->` chain. A step moves a status with `-.->` only, and no status leads to a step. A status move is no way out of a step, so an end may move the last status and stay an end. Every status after the first is reached by a step's move, and a status never takes the accent
94	- **A body at `Balanced` or `Faithful`.** A `%% detail:` line needs `%% level: balanced` or `%% level: faithful`, names a plain step `[Label]` that is no status, and holds 1 to 4 lines at Balanced and 1 to 10 at Faithful, each of 44 characters or fewer
95	- **Notes on zones and lanes.** A `%% about:` line names a lane or a zone, holds 1 to 3 lines of 56 characters or fewer, and every `%% zone:` stage of a process at `Balanced` or `Faithful` carries one
96	- **A reason for the accent.** The styled step or decision takes `%% focus: <id> because <reason>`, at most 30 characters, which the key draws as `In focus: <reason>`
97	- The shared rules: labels, quoting, ids, no emoji or markup, exactly one `style` line from `references/style-guide.md`, one direction for every process diagram in the file
98	
99	Judged by hand:
100	
101	- **No node returns to itself.** A connector from a node back onto the same node draws no loop a reader can follow, so a retry goes into a label or through the node it returns through, and `scripts/flow_check.py` refuses one
102	- **A handoff is the edge that matters most.** When the process has lanes, a connector that crosses lanes is a handoff, and the step in focus is the sending step of the handoff that adds the most delay or risk
103	- **One owner per step.** A step two teams share is two steps or a handoff
104	- **Every non-rectangle shape earns its place.** A store that only one step touches may be a label on that step instead
105	- **A queue between two lanes is the handoff.** A queue that only carries work from one lane to the next adds nothing the crossing connector's label cannot say, so it fails the remove test and is drawn as that label, such as `Claim queued`. It is a store only when the source treats it as a place steps read and write on their own, such as a ticket tool
106	- **Lanes follow the order work first reaches them,** top to bottom or left to right
107	- **No diagram carries the same label on four or more connectors.** Cut them all, or keep one where the label says something the shape cannot. A decision's exits are the exception, because they read the same way through the process
108	
109	---
110	
111	## 4. BUDGET AND SPLITTING
112	
113	Over budget, cut in sk-design-diagram's degrade order and stop as soon as the diagram fits: notes and decoration first, then exact duplicates merged into one step, then steps that change nothing a reader decides, then cross-cutting steps such as logging. Still over, split into an overview, with each phase as one subroutine step, and one detail diagram per phase. When the user asked in so many words for one board, cut the next item in that order instead, name it under `Left out:` and offer the split as the alternative in the playback. Everything cut is named under `Left out:`. At `Meeting screen` distance labels drop to 32 characters. At `Wall` distance the budget drops to 6 nodes and 8 connectors, or 8 nodes and 11 connectors with lanes, with labels at 25 characters, as the reading distance dial in `references/flow-mode.md` Section 4 sets out.
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 5. COLOUR, ZONES AND NOTES
118	
119	The composer colours every step by its kind. A user flow and a process each carry exactly one `style` line, which marks the first glance. A styled failing end or decision keeps its kind and takes the accent's outline. The goal is named by a `%% goal:` line rather than styled. A styled step is drawn in the accent's pair. The line marks meaning: on an end, in light red, it marks a failure, and on a step it puts that step in focus. Figma's guidance gives every subgraph a different tint, and sk-design-diagram keeps containers neutral so the marked step stays the strongest signal. The composer takes both: each lane gets its own tint by the zone rule in `references/style-guide.md` Section 2, pale enough that a lane reads as a container and never as a mark. Notes on a step, such as a service level or a failure rate, go on through `references/hybrid-workflow.md`.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## 6. WRITING THE BOARD
124	
125	`scripts/compose_board.py` composes the model and one `use_figma` call draws the board, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 6 sets out. On the generated fallback, `generate_diagram` takes `name`, `mermaidSyntax` and `userIntent`, and no `useArchitectureLayoutCode`. The `fj` route draws a process only when it has no lanes and uses only the four user-flow shapes, because `fj` has no container verb and its shape types for a store, a sub-process or data were never confirmed. Any other process needs a hosted route.
126	
127	---
128	
129	## 7. READ-BACK
130	
131	Count nodes, connectors, labelled decision exits and lanes, and check that each step sits inside its lane's section on the board.
132	
133	The lane order is compared as well, because the check counts the lanes and never reads their order. Walk the lanes in the order work first reaches them, top to bottom on `TD` and left to right on `LR`, and compare that walk with the order the model declares. A lane out of order is a mismatch, reported as measured like any other, and the order the lanes are declared in the model is what fixes it.
134	
135	```text
136	Read-back: 11 of 11 nodes, 12 of 12 connectors, 2 of 2 decision exits labelled, 3 of 3 lanes
137	```
138	
139	A status lane counts as a lane, and its statuses as nodes. Its order is read too: the status lane sits first, and its statuses run in the order the chain joins them. A detail card counts as one node, and its body is compared line by line with the model's `%% detail:` line.
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 8. PATTERNS AND EXAMPLE
144	
145	- `assets/templates/process.md` holds a decision tree, a laned process and a pipeline with a store
146	- `assets/examples/process-fernhouse-refund.md` walks a laned refund process from a support runbook to the reply
147	- `assets/examples/process-fernhouse-commission.md` walks a laned process with a status lane and detail cards, a client and a maker moving one commission through its statuses

2	title: "FigJam Diagram Quality Rubric"
3	description: "The taste gate a FigJam model passes before the write gate, translated from sk-design-diagram's success criteria: type fit, the remove test, signal, the check, the board, the design rubric that scores a composed board and the reply."
4	contextType: implementation
5	importance_tier: important
6	trigger_phrases:
7	  - "figjam quality rubric"
8	  - "diagram taste gate"
9	  - "remove test"

12	version: 1.0.13.0
13	---
14	
15	# FigJam Diagram Quality Rubric
16	
17	The script checks what a script can see. This rubric is the rest: whether the diagram should exist, whether every node earns its place and whether the reader can trust what lands on the board. Walk it after the check passes and before the write gate.
18	
19	**Loading Condition:** CONDITIONAL, on every Flow route before the write gate
20	**Purpose:** The judgement pass between the pre-write check and the gate
21	**Scope:** The model, the provenance table, the planned extensions and, after the write, the board and the reply
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 1. TYPE FIT
26	
27	- [ ] The type answers the reader's question, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 3 maps it
28	- [ ] A table, a list or a paragraph would not do the same job. If it would, say so and offer that instead
29	- [ ] The type's reference in `references/types/` was loaded and its judged-by-hand rules were applied
30	- [ ] A request for a kind Flow Mode does not draw was answered with the nearest type it does draw, or a plain no
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 2. THE REMOVE TEST
35	
36	sk-design-diagram's highest-quality move is usually deletion. A diagram is done when nothing can be removed.
37	
38	The remove test runs on the outline before the first Mermaid block, because a step cut from a list of steps costs a sentence and the same step cut from a drawn diagram costs a redraw. This section is the third rung of the challenge ladder in `references/flow-mode.md` Section 3, so the two rungs above it are asked first: what the board must not do, and whether a list, a table or a paragraph would serve the reader better.
39	
40	- [ ] The `userIntent` sentence was agreed in the sparring and is the first line of the outline, rather than composed at the write call
41	- [ ] The remove test ran on the outline, one line per node and edge, before any layout was judged
42	- [ ] An unanswered sparring proposal is marked assumed and named in the playback before the gate
43	- [ ] No node can be removed without the reader losing a step they need
44	- [ ] Every node serves the `userIntent` sentence, or it is cut and named under `Left out:`
45	- [ ] No two nodes always travel together. If they do, they are one node
46	- [ ] No connector restates what the layout already shows
47	- [ ] No label repeats what the shape already says
48	- [ ] No diagram carries the same label on four or more connectors. Cut them all, or keep one where the label says something the shape cannot. Decision exits and sequence messages are exempt, and an architecture renames each edge instead, as its type reference sets out
49	- [ ] The remove test ran on the outline before the first Mermaid block, so no node was drawn only to be cut
50	- [ ] The diagram sits inside its budget, or was split, and every cut is named under `Left out:`
51	- [ ] The board teaches what its source says beyond the request: where the source holds the options a screen offers, the rule a step applies or where a stage starts and ends, the board carries it in a body or a zone note, so a reader answers a question the request's first sentence does not
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 3. SIGNAL
56	
57	The marked node is chosen against a target written down first. A board judged only against itself cannot catch a second focal object, such as a title that repeats the claim the marked node was meant to carry. Three lines are written before the first Mermaid block:

# FigJam Process Templates

Copy/apply patterns for a process model. Each pattern passes `scripts/flow_check.py`, and `references/types/process.md` holds the rules.

**Loading Condition:** CONDITIONAL, with `references/types/process.md`
**Purpose:** Starting points for a process or decision flowchart
**Scope:** Four patterns. The provenance table and the reply shape are in `assets/flow-templates.md`

---

## 1. USAGE

- Keep the `%% type: process` line first, or the check reads the block as a user flow
- Name a lane after the actor, `subgraph agent ["CS agent"]`, and keep its id short and camelCase
- A lane takes the neutral pair or no style, and the one accent goes on the focal step, such as the step that hands work to the next lane. The composer draws that step in focus. A `linkStyle` passes the check and changes nothing on a composed board
- `-.->` marks a step that is optional or proposed. A log write that runs today is drawn solid
- The patterns all run left to right, because the check reads every process in one file as one flow that runs one way

---

## 2. PATTERNS

### Decision tree

```mermaid
%% type: process
flowchart LR
    %% goal: done
    start([Request in]) --> size{Over the limit?}
    size -->|No| auto[Approve automatically]
    size -->|Yes| risk{Known customer?}
    risk -->|Yes| review[Manager reviews]
    risk -->|No| reject([Declined])
    auto --> done([Approved])
    review --> done
    style size fill:#FFC2EC,stroke:#F849C1
    %% focus: size because the limit splits the path
```

### Laned process with a handoff in focus

The step that hands work to operations is in focus, because that handoff adds the most delay.

```mermaid
%% type: process
flowchart LR
    subgraph requester ["Requester"]
        ask([Request sent])
    end
    subgraph team ["Support team"]
        triage{Complete?}
        more[Ask for details]
        approve[Approve]
    end
    subgraph ops ["Operations"]
        fulfil[Fulfil the request]
        closed([Request closed])
    end
    ask --> triage
    triage -->|No| more
    more --> triage
    triage -->|Yes| approve
    approve --> fulfil
    fulfil --> closed
    style requester fill:#F5F5F5,stroke:#B3B3B3
    style team fill:#F5F5F5,stroke:#B3B3B3
    style ops fill:#F5F5F5,stroke:#B3B3B3
    style approve fill:#C2E5FF,stroke:#3DADFF
    %% focus: approve because it hands off to ops
```

### Laned process with a status lane and detail cards

A client and a maker move one record through its statuses. The status lane is declared first, each status move is a dotted `-.->` and the `Faithful` level gives one step a body.

```mermaid
%% type: process
flowchart LR
    %% status: status
    %% level: faithful
    %% detail: start | Checks the order form | Replies within two working days
    subgraph status ["Order status"]
        open[Open]
        made[In the making]
        done[Delivered]
    end
    subgraph client ["Client"]
        ask([Order placed])
        got([Order received])
    end
    subgraph maker ["Maker"]
        start[Start the work]
        ship[Ship the order]
    end
    open --> made
    made --> done
    ask --> start
    ask -.-> open
    start -.-> made
    start --> ship
    ship -.-> done
    ship --> got
    style ship fill:#C2E5FF,stroke:#3DADFF
    %% focus: ship because it moves the order
```

### Pipeline with a store and data in and out

```mermaid
%% type: process
flowchart LR
    %% goal: done
    upload[/Upload a file/] --> parse[Parse rows]
    parse --> valid{Rows valid?}
    valid -->|Yes| save[Save the import]
    valid -->|No| errors[/Error report/]
    save --> store[(Imports)]
    save -->|"Later"| notify[[Notify the owner]]
    notify --> done([Import finished])
    style valid fill:#FFC2EC,stroke:#F849C1
    %% focus: valid because bad rows stop the import
```
